Summer at the lake? These New England lakes are best for fun in the sun

From the lakes and ponds of Maine to the shores New Hampshire's Lake Winnipesaukee, these are the best New England lakes for summer fun.
Posted by by Courtney Elko
Lake Winnipesaukee in the Lakes Region of New Hampshire (Photo: @kayp via Twenty20)

This post was last updated and reviewed for accuracy on July 31, 2026 by Beth Luberecki.

Sure, New England is beautiful in the fall. But the northeastern corner of the United States is also home to some of the country’s most idyllic lakes perfect for summer family vacations. And with fishing, swimming, boating, hiking, mountain biking, moose safaris, and even a few outdoor water parks nearby to keep families entertained, there’s no shortage of things to do on a family vacation at New England’s best lakes.

From the peaceful waterways of Maine’s Moosehead Lake to the summer tourism hub of Lake Winnipesaukee in New Hampshire, these are the best New England lakes and lake towns for summer vacation fun. 

AT THE WATER’S EDGE: The best lakefront resorts in the U.S. for families

Lake Winnipesaukee, New Hampshire

At more than 44,500 acres (72 square miles), Lake Winnipesaukee isn’t just the largest lake in New Hampshire. It’s also one of the most enduringly popular family getaway spots in all of New England, drawing families from across the region with its seemingly endless variety of public beaches, boat launches, fishing spots, and swimming areas.

AFFORDABLE FUN: 11 affordable family vacation destinations in the U.S.: FamilyVacationist’s 2026 guide

The 81-mile loop drive around Lake Winnipesaukee takes you through the towns of Meredith, Wolfeboro, Center Harbor, Moultonborough, Tuftonboro, Alton, Gilford, and Laconia, offering plenty of spots along the way for scenic views and touristy stops. In Laconia, Weirs Beach is a popular swimming spot with a bathhouse and playground. Shopping, dining, waterslides, miniature golf, go-karts, arcades, art galleries, boardwalks, and scenic boat rides are among the other favorite activities in the Winnipesaukee area. Fireworks and outdoor performances are common in the summer months as well.

Boat tours operated by Mount Washington Cruises are a great way to see the lake up close, especially for skip-gen travel or multigenerational family vacations where some family members may need to take it a bit slower. A ride on the Winnipesaukee Railway is a similarly paced activity and a pleasant way to spend a morning or afternoon.

Where to stay near Lake Winnipesaukee

Half Moon Motel and Cottages is centrally located to Weirs Beach in Laconia. It’s within walking distance to the boardwalk, train station, and public beach. Families love the big outdoor pool and Lake Winnipesaukee views. The cottages are ideal for family stays and come with a fully equipped kitchenette.

Mill Falls Resort Collection at the Lake offers four different lodging options in one, including a rustically elegant Adirondack-style inn. The all-season resort offers family-friendly amenities and activities like weekend campfires with s’mores, pontoon boat charters, lawn games, and watercraft rentals. 

Lake Champlain, Vermont

Bordering New York, Vermont, and the Canadian province of Quebec, Lake Champlain is a serene freshwater lake with a relatively undeveloped coastline capped by the quirky coastal town of Burlington, Vermont, on its eastern shore.

Opportunities for typical outdoor lake activities like fishing, boating, swimming, and water sports are abundant here, and many of the area’s coastal hikes feature short, easy trails with breathtaking Lake Champlain views. When you tire of the outdoors, head to downtown Burlington for shops, eateries, and a thriving arts scene complete with street vendors and music festivals.

Where to stay near Lake Champlain

Pet-friendly Hotel Vermont in downtown Burlington is within walking distance of Lake Champlain and offers kid-friendly touches like complimentary bedtime stories for the little ones. Book the Kids & Family Package and young travelers are welcomed to their room with a tray of milk and cookies, coloring pages, and a menu of games the hotel can deliver for a family game night.

Newly opened for summer 2026, The Harborvale, Autograph Collection sits between the shores of Lake Champlain and downtown Burlington. The dog-friendly property features an indoor pool, fitness center, and programming like a lakeside scavenger hunt for kids and daily sunset toasts.

Moosehead Lake, Maine

There’s no mystery to how Moosehead Lake got its name: The 40-mile, 75,000-acre body of water in northwestern Maine really is shaped like a moose’s head. And considering that moose outnumber people by three to one in the region, you’ll have an excellent chance of spotting one of these magnificent animals in the wild here, too. (You can increase your odds by taking a professional moose safari and wildlife tour.)

FAMILY TRIPS: 11 most charming seaside towns and villages in New England

Moosehead Lake is the largest mountain lake in the eastern United States and the source of Maine’s serene Kennebec River. You can explore the area on your own or hire a Registered Maine Guide to show you all the best spots. Natural pursuits here include fishing, boating, swimming, whitewater rafting, and kayaking.

Where to stay near Moosehead Lake

The pet-friendly Lodge at Moosehead Lake boasts lake views from its guest rooms and a large outdoor firepit for communal fun. The Mt. Kineo Suite is ideal for families, as it can sleep up to five people with two bedrooms and a rollaway bed. There’s also a fully equipped kitchen, gas fireplace, and large private deck in the suite.

The only Relais & Châteaux Hotel & Restaurant in Maine, Blair Hill Inn makes for a luxe lakeside escape. Ten guest rooms and six cabins sit amid 79 acres on a hillside perch, where guests can enjoy a fine-dining restaurant, full-service spa, private hiking trails, and trout pond.

Candlewood Lake, Connecticut 

Situated within the 11-acre Candlewood Lake Town Park, Candlewood Lake is the largest lake in the state of Connecticut and a perfect beachside spot for swimming, boating, and fishing. Families love the lake’s playground, picnic tables, boat dock, and concession stand.

Golf courses and kid-friendly mini-golf courses abound not far from Candlewood Lake, and the nearby Bear Mountain Reservation offers 140 acres of green space and hiking trails, including portions with lake views. Families also enjoy exploring the Danbury Railway Museum and the Danbury Fair Mall, an upscale shopping mall with dozens of stores, a carousel, and children’s play area. 

Where to stay near Candlewood Lake

With an outdoor firepit seating area, fitness center, and on-site restaurant open for breakfast and dinner, the Hilton Garden Inn Danbury is a smart choice for families staying near Candlewood Lake.  

Courtyard by Marriott Danbury is another great hotel option for families, with an outdoor firepit, 24-hour fitness center, and indoor heated pool. Refreshed rooms all include mini-fridges, and breakfast and dinner are available at the on-site restaurant.

Rangeley Lake, Maine

Nestled within Maine’s mountainous backcountry, Rangeley Lake is one of six pristine bodies of water collectively known as the Rangeley Lakes region. Vacationing families visit to experience the dual benefits of lake and mountain activities. Shadowed by nearby Saddleback Mountain, the 6,000-acre lake offers endless opportunities for fishing, swimming, bird-watching, and boating, with boat launches available in Rangeley Lake State Park. The state park also offers plenty of kid-friendly hiking trails, picnic spots, and campsites. 

Take a drive around the region on the 35-mile Rangeley Lakes National Scenic Byway and you may just spot a moose. Downtown Rangeley is a quintessential New England town filled with shops and eateries. A variety of festivals also lure visitors throughout the summer months. 

Where to stay near Rangeley Lake

Located on the easterly shore of Rangeley Lake, Loon Lodge Inn and Restaurant offers lakeside views and spectacular sunsets. Built in 1899, the Loon Lodge features boat slips at its dock, its own swimming beach, and parking for RVs. Guest rooms come with a mini-fridge and air-conditioning, but no telephones or televisions are available in the rooms because, well, nobody really visits Rangeley for TV or the internet. 

Book a two- or three-bedroom log cabin at pet-friendly Rangeley Lake Resort and enjoy access to amenities like a heated swimming pool, cedar sauna, fitness facility, and game room. Every cabin has a full kitchen, making a family vacation even easier.  

Lake Sunapee, New Hampshire

Western New Hampshire’s 4,100-acre Lake Sunapee is surrounded by state parks, including Mount Sunapee State Park, where families come to enjoy one of the best family beaches in New England (complete with lifeguards, boat rentals, a playground, restrooms, and campsites). In addition to fishing, swimming, golfing, and camping, the Sunapee Lake area is a prime spot for family-friendly hiking and mountain biking trails.

Where to stay near Lake Sunapee

Within easy walking distance of Mount Sunapee State Park Beach, the Mountain Edge Suites at Sunapee has two indoor pools, a game room, and complimentary daily continental breakfast. The hotel’s one- and two-bedroom guest rooms come with kitchenettes.

The Lodge Hotel by Sunapee Stays offers 11 Adirondack-themed suites with large kitchenettes and semi-private patios with mountain views. A game and movie room, outdoor pool, and firepit provide opportunities for family fun.

Lake Bomoseen, Vermont

The largest lake entirely within Vermont’s borders, Lake Bomoseen is a popular spot for boating, fishing, and swimming. You can do all of that at Bomoseen State Park, which offers canoe, kayak, rowboat, and pedal boat rentals along with several hiking trails, including one that connects to Half Moon Pond State Park.

You can also swim and rent kayaks at Crystal Beach on the east side of the lake or book a guided fishing tour to see what’s biting. Take a scenic trail ride at Pond Hill Ranch, or bike past villages, farms, and fields along the Delaware & Hudson Rail Trail.

Where to stay near Lake Bomoseen

Lake Bomoseen Lodge offers a selection of fully renovated lodge rooms, condos, and cottages perched by its namesake lake, some of which are pet-friendly. Swim at the pool and beach area, sit around a firepit, or head to the on-site taproom for brews and eats with a view.

For outdoorsy families, Lake Bomoseen State Park has 55 tent/RV sites and 10 lean-to sites. Some campsites are wooded; others are located right along the lakeshore.

Sebago Lake, Maine

The second-largest lake in Maine, Sebago Lake has plenty of fans in Southern Maine yet still can feel uncrowded. Sebago Lake State Park sits at its northeast corner, offering beaches, boat launches, picnic areas, and lakeside camping. Tassel Top Beach and Nason’s Beach and Campground are two other options for swimming and sunning by the water.

It’s easy to rent kayaks, paddleboards, and motor boats if you don’t have your own. Float-plane excursions are another fun way to explore the lake, albeit from a different vantage point. Sebago Lake’s also a great place to see what’s biting; brook trout, black crappie, large-mouth and small-mouth bass, and white and yellow perch can be found around its inlets, coves, underwater islands, and rock piles. And because it’s one of the state’s deepest lakes, lake trout also thrive there.

Where to stay near Sebago Lake

Migis Lodge on Sebago Lake, one of the best all-inclusive resorts in the U.S., has been drawing families and multigenerational groups for more than 100 years. The resort makes it easy to get out on Sebago Lake with water sports like waterskiing, wakeboarding, kayaking, and paddleboarding, and other activities include tennis, pickleball, disc golf, and kids camp programming.

Enjoy the throwback vacation vibes at Sebago Lake Lodge & Cottages, which sits on a point of land that juts out into Sebago Lake in Standish, Maine. The property boasts more than 700 feet of lake frontage, with swimming and boat docking areas and complimentary canoes and kayaks for paddling around the area.

Lake Mansfield, Massachusetts 

The Berkshires’ small-but-serene Lake Mansfield may technically be a pond, but this 29-acre slice of paradise has plenty of room for swimming, fishing, boating, and canoeing. There’s a quarter-mile walking loop trail that’s perfect for spotting local wildlife in the area.

When you want to kickstart your morning with some exercise, lakeside yoga classes are held three times a week in July and August. Downtown Great Barrington, less than five minutes from the lake, offers an arts and cultural district filled with shops, art galleries, theaters, and eateries. 

Where to stay near Lake Mansfield

The Fairfield by Marriott Inn & Suites Great Barrington Lenox/Berkshires, just minutes from Lake Mansfield, is ideally suited for families. The hotel has an indoor pool, game room, and complimentary hot breakfast, and all guest rooms come with a microwave and mini-fridge. Studio guest rooms have two queen beds and a sleeper sofa, perfect for families of five.

A well-reviewed budget-friendly pick, Monument Mountain Motel offers vintage vacation vibes and amenities like in-room microwaves and fridges, barbecue facilities, and a picnic area.

Worden Pond, Rhode Island

Despite its name, Rhode Island’s Worden Pond is considered a lake. And, at more than 1,000 acres, it’s a fairly big one by New England standards—big, but not deep. Because Worden Pond averages a depth of just four feet, there’s excellent fishing to be had here year-round. Perch, bluegill, and sunfish abound in this Rhode Island lake.

Where to stay near Worden Pond

Worden Pond is an especially good New England lake destination for RV road trips, and if you’re traveling by RV, the family-owned and -operated Worden Pond Family Campground is the place to stay. Along with RV parking and hookups, the campground has a picnic table and fire ring at each station, plus community restrooms and showers. There are also basketball and volleyball courts, a horseshoe pit, and a playground. 

If you’d prefer a hotel, Hampton Inn South Kingstown is a good choice for families, with an indoor pool, complimentary daily breakfast, and a location convenient to Worden Pond as well as other local attractions like Adventureland Family Fun Park and Narragansett Town Beach.

Lake Quinsigamond, Massachusetts 

Just an hour west of Boston, Lake Quinsigamond and the surrounding Quinsigamond State Park offer the perfect mix of city getaway and New England lake vacation. With opportunities for fishing, non-motorized boating, sailing, and swimming, there’s no shortage of water-based activities here, and the surrounding state park boasts plenty of picnic areas, tennis courts, and walking or running trails. Lake Quinsigamond is also famous for its rowing competitions, and regattas are popular here throughout the rowing season.

Beyond the lake, the nearby EcoTarium in Worcester is a popular science and nature museum that caters to kids and families. Fit for all ages, this interactive indoor-outdoor children’s center features live animal habitats, hikes through forests and nature trails, and a seasonal train ride around its 45-acre campus.

Where to stay near Lake Quinsigamond

The all-suite Residence Inn by Marriott Worcester has a state-of-the-art fitness center, on-site pickleball court, and complimentary daily hot breakfast buffet. All of the recently renovated suites also feature a fully equipped kitchen.

The only AAA Four Diamond hotel in Central Massachusetts, Beechwood Hotel is just a short walk away from Lake Quinsigamond. Some guest rooms are pet friendly, and the on-site Sonoma Restaurant offers indoor and outdoor seating.

Winnapaug Pond, Rhode Island

Separated from the Atlantic Ocean by a large sandbar, Winnapaug Pond (actually a 2.5-mile saltwater lake on the coast of Rhode Island) is known for its calm waters compared to the popular nearby Misquamicut State Beach. Winnapaug Pond’s shallow depths are ideal for kayaking. 

After a day on the water, make sure to explore the landmark Atlantic Beach Park, which is situated on the same sandbar barrier. Atlantic Beach Park, which offers amusement rides for younger children and classic arcade games, first opened in 1921. But the most popular and traditional thing to do at the park is to take a spin on the historic flying horse carousel. Summer isn’t complete otherwise! 

Where to stay near Winnapaug Pond

Just 10 minutes from Winnapaug Pond, the Ocean House is a high-end beachfront hotel that offers food and arts experiences, croquet clinics, fitness classes, afternoon movie screenings, and evenings around the firepit.

Blue Whale Inn offers deluxe suites ideal for families or larger groups, as well as amenities like a playground and complimentary use of beach chairs and umbrellas.
